query: What is the right of private defence under Section 34?

gold_references.label: Section 34
gold_references.role: things done in private defence are not offences

gold_references.label: Section 35
gold_references.role: scope of the right of private defence of body and property

required_points: Section 34 states that nothing is an offence which is done in the exercise of the right of private defence.

Section 35 elaborates that every person has the right, subject to restrictions, to defend their own body, any other person's body, and their own or another's property against theft, robbery, mischief, or criminal trespass.
optional_points: The right is subject to restrictions in Section 37, including that there must be no time to seek public authority protection.
forbidden_points: Private defence is an unlimited right to use any force.
Private defence can only be used for self-protection and not for protection of another person.

notes: Direct lookup. Section 34 is the foundational private defence provision.
